title: Rollout Sample Surgeon Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc (scratch notes + templates) for performing small, surgical sample exposures during cross-functional rollouts and A/B experiments. The framing here is intentionally clinical: pick minimal, well-instrumented cohorts, perform a measured incision, monitor deeply, then close/recover quickly.

Audience:
- Product managers coordinating feature activation
- Release engineers running traffic routing
- Observability and SRE on-call leads
- Solutions and customer-facing engineers for private/dedicated customers

High-level pattern (one line):
Pick microcohort -> small spike exposure -> targeted telemetry + qualitative checks -> decision within 1–6 hours -> either expand, hold, or revert.

Key principles (for guild alignment):
- Minimal blast radius: never exceed 1% of target MAU for initial incision unless explicit business justification.
- Fast feedback loop: instrument to get meaningful signals in < 60 minutes where possible.
- Hypothesis-first: every exposure must state the hypothesis and the primary/secondary signals that will confirm or refute it.
- Ownership and tempo: designate a single steward (the Sample Surgeon) who is empowered to cut or suture (route or revert) without multi-channel approval during the first hour.

Experiment taxonomy (useful shorthand):
- Microcanary: single feature flag route, <0.5% traffic, focus on error/sla regressions.
- Signal Hunt: small slice for behavioral drift (semantic/regression quality), often uses targeted prompts or heuristics.
- Throughput Probe: short-duration traffic spike to validate autoscaling and tail latency.
- Cohort A/B: planned randomized split for metrics evaluation; start with tiny weights and ramp.

Pre-launch checklist (before traffic is cut):
- Owner assigned (Sample Surgeon): name + mobile + slack handle.
- Primary hypothesis (one sentence).
- Primary signal (single metric): e.g., 99th latency, failed-rank-rate, or precision@k change on reranker.
- Secondary signals: cost/unit, token counts, error codes distribution, user-reported defects.
- Safety enveloped thresholds: precise numeric trigger values for automated rollback and human alert tiers.
- Telemetry baked in: synthetic transactions, canary-specific tags, tracing spans with trace sampling 100% for first 60m.
- Canary traffic orchestration ready: rollout config in console, pre-signed rollback command, and runbook link.
- Stakeholder inform: oncall, product, data-science, and legal (if enterprise cohort) notified.
- Dry-run runbook: simulated routing test, verify metrics pipeline for canary tag.

Example numeric guardrails (starter suggestions):
- Start weight: 0.1% of global traffic or 50–200 requests/min for low volume endpoints.
- Max initial window: 2 hours (unless mission-critical requires shorter).
- Auto-rollback: if 5xx rate increases by > 2x AND absolute 5xx delta > 0.2% in 10m window.
- Human interrupt: any user-facing correctness regression > 2 points on domain eval or critical customer report.
- Cost cap: expected token spend for initial window with 2x margin; if exceeded, auto-throttle.

Sampling heuristics (how to choose cohorts):
- Orthogonal slices over naive geography: prefer behavioral or funnel-based slices (new users, search-heavy, single-session power-users).
- Small-batch stratification: ensure sample contains at least 3 device types and 2 major client versions to avoid device-specific regressions.
- Exclude sensitive enterprise tenants by default; if included, require explicit opt-in and legal signoff.
- Use a deterministic hash on user_id % 10000 to allocate stable microcohorts across runs.

Telemetry and signal deck (what to monitor first):
1) System health:  p95/p99 latency, successRate, GPU queue depth, instance spin-up times.
2) Quality regressions: model-eval drift score, rerank swap rate, hallucination proxy heuristics (policy-based detectors).
3) Cost and throughput: tokens/server, cost per 1k tokens, unexpected burst in I/O.
4) Observability coverage: sampling rates, trace completeness, and presence of canary tags in logs.
5) Business KPIs: conversion, engagement delta, rollback impact.

Decision cadence and choreography:
- T+0: cut traffic to initial microweight, confirm routing & tags (10m).
- T+10: first telemetry sweep (health only) -> if failing auto-rollback.
- T+30: quality checks + data-science quick eval on sample; run small human review if ambiguous.
- T+60–120: expanded telemetry correlation (error types, user flows), decide expand/hold/revert.

Comms templates (short):
- Slack alert (automated): "[CANARY] feature=X weight=0.1% cut by @asha — primary signal: p99 latency. Auto-rollback: enabled. Runbook: <link>"
- Human escalation: "Escalation: canary X crossing p99 threshold by 2x at 10:23 UTC. Please join #rollout-incident and stand by for decision."

Incident scripts (quick ops steps):
- If auto-rollback triggered: identify affected clients (tag), issue rollback route change, run synthetic smoke tests, confirm metric recovery for 2 consecutive 1-min windows, then triage.
- If quality regression: pause routing immediately, capture 100% traces for 30m, snapshot model and config versions, collect failed examples for DS triage.
- If oscillation (flapping between states): hold at 0.1% and disable autoscale for experiment lane until root cause found.

Post-mortem/lightweight analysis checklist (after decision):
- Export canary telemetry window and baseline window.
- Sample of N failed/changed predictions with context.
- Cost analysis and variance from forecast.
- Action items: revert permanent, patch fix, or safe expansion plan. Owner + ETA for each item.

Templates and small utilities (practical):
- Quick hash assignment snippet (pseudo): user_cohort = hash(user_id) % 10000; if user_cohort < 10 -> microcanary
- Synthetic test set doc link: (add link to canonical prompt set for targeted drift checks).
- Small spreadsheet fields to capture: window_start, window_end, p50,p95,p99,5xx_rate,model_swap_rate,token_spend,notes

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Create a lightweight canary-dashboard template in console for the Sample Surgeon role.
- Define standard synthetic prompt sets per product vertical (search vs. reply vs. composing).
- Align on stable hash allocation between hosted and private deployments so private customers can mirror a rollout in staging.
- Formalize decision authority matrix for enterprise slices that cross contractual SLAs.

Quick reference: short checklist for the Sample Surgeon before cut (minimum):
1) Hypothesis stated
2) Runbook accessible
3) Telemetry tags working
4) Stakeholders paged
5) Auto-rollback enabled with numeric thresholds
6) Synthetic smoke test ready
7) Rollback/playbook command tested

Notes (informal):
- This doc is intentionally terse — it's a surgical checklist + pattern language. Keep it updated as we learn new failure modes.
- If you are oncall and the Sample Surgeon isn't reachable, follow the auto-rollback and then escalate to the product lead in the current oncall roster.
- We should avoid overfitting guardrails to a single model; prefer percentile-relative thresholds where possible.

References and attached artifacts:
- This sits alongside the broader rollout play materials in /product/console-and-rollouts. See linked artifacts above.
- Add results of the next 3 microcanaries here as appendices once we run them.

END OF NOTES

(rough, but practical — A.K.)
